protocol.purpose: Compare contact semantics at the previously observed adult-starvation window; no death-based stop or survival guarantee.
protocol.selection: Chosen from the completed previous study before these comparison outcomes.
protocol.scope: Both keep the complete interacting world. A single selected day is neither a historical death share nor seasonal viability. Subsequent phase hooks require an exact uninstrumented world reference.

referenceDay: The preselected adult-death day of the preceding 32.427-day survival continuation; not the original historical-law trajectory.

after.sourceOrigin: frozen working tree; match final implementation commit before publication

camp.name: Amber Hollow
camp.interpretation: Population, not stock volume, sets this snapshot footprint. Camp biomass is an aggregate finite stock reachable only from these footprint/access cells under the current approximation; no individual warehouse, distance-dependent carrying, or ownership change is inferred.

limits: One starting snapshot cannot prove actual movement or stationarity during any subsequent work interval.
No donor availability trajectory, willingness frequency, achieved work, treatment effect, or prevented-death share is inferred.
Current local food choice is conditional on prior care opportunities and individual random/learned decisions. No choices or RNG were evaluated.
The sole substantive holder may consume her apparent surplus in the physiological/refill phases before a food-work snapshot; no future interval was advanced.
Read-only analyst access to saved quantities is not information granted to inhabitants.
Unwatched neighbors include people selected solely for same rounded occupied cell; same-cell presence remains a coarse contact model, not anatomical reach.
Projected cells and static BFS access are model approximations; no new physical capacity, material allocation, path or stock was created.
The pending-route source defect is established independently; these snapshot data do not show it caused or could prevent any of the 16 subsequent deaths.

controlledDefect.baselineTest: The unchanged previous runtime passes an explicitly stopped recipient but fails the same physically stranded recipient with a pending route.
controlledDefect.candidate: Both actor orders permit finite paid handoff to either stationary recipient; ingestion and regained motion occur only in later physiology.
negativeControls: Actual positive travel invalidates contact even after returning to the initial coordinates.
Blocked and zero-distance routes retain stationary contact.
Travel cannot earn harvesting on arrival.
Absent, unwilling, unfunded or distant donors grant no food.
Removed/replaced bodies cannot share finite resources.

interpretation: The physical contact defect is reproduced and corrected; this selected full-world comparison prevents none of the 16 adult deaths.
All 16 still receive no handoff or covering work, ingest/oxidize no food or reserves, and perform no funded movement during the traced window. They have no selected accessible shared source.
One adult dies three ticks (45 simulated minutes) earlier. Its trace differs in sickness; broader behavioral/RNG divergence is not an independently apportioned cause.
The nearby stock census covers only the initial checkpoint. Digested intake and internal reserves are not transferable provisions. Presence, stock and willingness remain distinct.
Whole-world and community food/injury changes are mixed; this is no seasonal or generational viability result.

The next material question is how the adults became cut off from renewable food, transport and care. Planned-but-unperformed work demand and developmental/thermal calibration require separate controls.
